content:
Hi!

I've built the AI safety formalization atlas: a Lean workbench for machine-checking AI-safety arguments. Lean/Mathlib v4.31.0, one root import import AISafetyAtlas.

The vision is to make it one place that enables work on formal AI safety, with many tools together. I'll be using it in my own work first, and I'd like it to be useful to others too.

I started with the low-hanging fruit so I reused existing rather than reproved: Gödel I/II, Tarski, Löb from Foundation, Chaitin from Milovanov, Arrow from CC Liang, Gibbard-Satterthwaite from SocialChoiceLean, Rice and halting over Mathlib. Licenses and pins are in the repo.

Mine: parts of Wolpert's No Free Lunch (finite cores - supervised off-training-set 1996, optimization 1997), plus a bridging layer tying the classics to verification questions, e.g. no total decider for behavioral safety of encoded agents, via Rice. Narrow on purpose, and no claim that any real system fits the model. No sorry, and CI checks the headline surface closes over only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

Now the plan is to (auto)formalize more interesting material, including work of mine that never got formalized, plus a few new conjectures that might be useful in the field. Lean helps enormously here compared to pen and paper.

Tiny entry task if you want to poke at it: issue #28. Feedback and contributions welcome.
